task: Fill cow horns with fresh cow manure and bury
steiner: Horns filled with cow manure are buried and kept in the soil over the winter, "when the earth is most vitalized".
practice: Bury in autumn. Later practice buries the horns while the Moon is descending ("planting time").
source: Steiner, Agriculture Course (GA 327), lecture 4; later practice

task: Dig up the horns
steiner: Dug up after the winter.
practice: Lifted in spring. No Moon rule is given in the sources.

task: Stir for one hour and spray onto the soil
steiner: Stirred for an hour, alternating the direction of the vortex.
practice: Sprayed in spring and autumn, in the late afternoon or evening, while the Moon is descending; preferably when the Moon is in an Earth constellation (Root day).
source: Steiner, Agriculture Course (GA 327), lecture 4; Biodynamic Agriculture Australia; Dyyna after von Wistinghausen; Biodynamic Trainee (Root days)

task: Fill cow horns with ground quartz paste and bury
steiner: Quartz ground to a fine powder, mixed into a thin paste, filled into horns and left in the soil over the summer.
practice: Buried in spring (TNAU: from March/April). No Moon rule is given in the sources.

task: Dig up the horns
steiner: Removed in late autumn and stored until the following spring.
practice: Lifted in autumn.

task: Stir for one hour and spray as a fine mist over the plants
steiner: Stirred for an hour and used for light spraying of the plants themselves.
practice: Sprayed early in the morning, around sunrise, while the Moon is ascending, ideally on the day type of the crop (the plant group chosen in the settings).
source: Steiner, Agriculture Course (GA 327), lecture 4; Biodynamic Agriculture Australia; Biodynamic Trainee; Valentines Farm

task: Pick the yarrow flowers
steiner: Yarrow flower heads (Achillea millefolium) are used.
practice: Picked in full flower, in the morning on a sunny day. Flower day and ascending Moon follow the app's harvest rule (after Thun).
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 5; Biodynamic Association (US) preparation manual; app rule (Flower day, ascending Moon)

task: Fill a stag's bladder and hang it in the sun
steiner: The filled bladder hangs "in a spot that gets as much sunlight as possible during the summer".
practice: Hung through the summer.

task: Take the bladder down and bury it
steiner: "When autumn comes, take it down and bury it not too deeply in the ground for the winter."
practice: Buried in autumn; later practice prefers a descending Moon.

task: Dig it up
steiner: Lifted after the winter.
practice: Lifted in spring.

task: Pick the chamomile flowers
steiner: Chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla) flower heads are used.
practice: Picked on a sunny morning when the flowers are open, from the end of May. Flower day and ascending Moon follow the app's harvest rule.
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 5; Biodynamic Trainee; app rule (Flower day, ascending Moon)

task: Fill cattle intestine ("sausages") and bury
steiner: The sausages lie "throughout the entire winter at a shallow depth in soil as rich in humus as possible".
practice: Buried in autumn; later practice prefers a descending Moon.
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 5; Biodynamic Association (UK); later practice

task: Dig them up
steiner: Lifted after the winter.
practice: Lifted in spring.

task: Cut the nettles
steiner: Stinging nettles are slightly wilted and pressed together.
practice: Cut around the start of flowering. Ascending Moon follows the app's harvest rule.
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 5; app rule (ascending Moon)

task: Bury the nettles (for a whole year)
steiner: Buried without an animal sheath, separated from the soil by a light layer of peat: "it must remain buried for one year".
practice: Buried in autumn and left until the following autumn; later practice prefers a descending Moon.

task: Dig it up (one year after burying)
steiner: Lifted after one year.
practice: Lifted in autumn, a year after burying.

task: Collect and crumble oak bark
steiner: Oak bark is chopped to a crumbly texture.
practice: Collected in autumn, when the skull is filled.

task: Fill a skull and bury it in a wet place
steiner: Buried not too deep, under peat, where rainwater flows (or in a barrel of plant sludge); it "must ideally last through fall and winter".
practice: Buried in autumn; later practice prefers a descending Moon.

task: Dig it up
steiner: Lifted after the winter.
practice: Lifted in spring.

task: Pick the dandelion flowers
steiner: The yellow flower heads are gathered and slightly wilted.
practice: Picked early in the morning, before the flowers open fully. Flower day and ascending Moon follow the app's harvest rule.
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 5; Steiner and Biodynamic Composting; app rule (Flower day, ascending Moon)

task: Wrap in cattle mesentery and bury
steiner: Sewn into a cattle sheath and buried "throughout the winter".
practice: Buried in autumn while the Moon is descending.
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 5; The Wine Idealist; Biodynamic Association (UK)

task: Dig it up
steiner: Taken out in the spring.
practice: Lifted in spring, at the same time as horn manure.

task: Pick the valerian flowers and press the juice
steiner: The flowers of Valeriana officinalis are pressed and the juice diluted "very heavily" in warm water; "one can do this at any time".
practice: Flowers picked in early summer and pressed straight away. Flower day and ascending Moon follow the app's harvest rule.
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 5; biodynamicsolutions.org; app rule (Flower day, ascending Moon)

task: Insert 502-506 into the heap and spray 507 over it
steiner: The prepared substances are added to the manure or compost; the diluted valerian juice is incorporated very gently.
practice: Whenever a heap is built: 502-506 go into separate holes, then 507 is stirred and sprinkled over the heap. No Moon rule is given in the sources; only the unfavourable times are avoided.
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 5; Biodynamic Association (US) preparation manual

task: Collect field horsetail
steiner: Equisetum arvense is used.
practice: The green summer shoots are collected and can be dried for tea.

task: Make the tea and spray it on the plants and soil
steiner: Made into "a fairly concentrated tea, which is then diluted" and sprayed against blight and similar diseases.
practice: Sprayed as a preventive in the few days leading up to Full Moon, from sunrise to mid-morning; especially useful when Full Moon falls near perigee (so perigee is not avoided here).
source: Steiner, GA 327, lecture 6; Biodynamic Association (UK); TNAU (2-4 days before Full Moon)
